title: Acid-fastness as a physical chemistry word
dek: Retention of dye after acid-alcohol. Wikipedia's property card. Mycolate envelope chemistry stays on tb-organism / tb-cell-envelope.
story: Acid-fastness on Wikipedia is a staining property, not a phylogeny: some organisms retain carbol fuchsin (or fluorochrome) after acid-alcohol because of a lipid-rich envelope.
Mycobacteria are the celebrity examples. Nocardia and some others can play too. That is why AFB ≠ Mtb on a smear.
The envelope chemistry that makes the property true in Mtb is already a Simplfy layered plate. This card is the word used in every methods sentence.
deep: Losing acid-fastness in some NTM or after some treatments is a stain comment, not a species change.
Auramine is a different dye with the same property idea.
Do not speciate from 'strong' versus 'weak' acid-fastness alone.
Cell-wall drug targets (INH, EMB) sit on the chemistry plates, not here.
